summary: Cuts and creases source geometry with a clipping plane, keeping primitives above, below, or on both sides of the plane.

key_params.name: clipop
key_params.note: Keep primitives above, below, or on both sides of the clipping plane.

key_params.name: dist
key_params.note: Offset the clipping plane along the direction vector.

key_params.name: dir
key_params.note: Normal vector defining the clipping plane orientation.

key_params.name: dirx
key_params.note: X component of the plane normal.

key_params.name: diry
key_params.note: Y component of the plane normal.

key_params.name: dirz
key_params.note: Z component of the plane normal.

key_params.name: newg
key_params.note: Create named groups for geometry above and below the plane when all primitives are kept.

key_params.name: above
key_params.note: Group name assigned through Create Groups for one side of the clipping plane.

key_params.name: below
key_params.note: Group name assigned through Create Groups for the other side of the clipping plane.

common_gotchas: Create Groups is only available when `clipop` is All Primitives / `both`.
The official `above` and `below` ids are both menu values and group-name parameter ids, so guard context matters.
Clip is a plane cut, not a solid Boolean; use Boolean SOP for closed-volume set operations.
key_concepts: Clip SOP is a plane-based cut and crease operation, not a closed-volume Boolean operation.
The `clipop` menu chooses whether to retain primitives above the plane, below the plane, or all generated primitives on both sides.
`dist` offsets the clipping plane along the `dir` normal vector, so diagonal or non-normalized directions change the cut orientation.
`newg` enables separate above/below output group names and is only available when `clipop` keeps all primitives.
